newsitem.title: USA: Jim Carrey carries day at MTV movie awards.
newsitem.headline: Jim Carrey carries day at MTV movie awards.

text.p: A deliriously foul-mouthed Jim Carrey stole the show at the seventh annual MTV Movie Awards on Saturday when he picked up two trophies for last year's box office disappointment, "The Cable Guy."

The bearded, rubber-faced comic was the only multiple winner at the irreverent ceremony, which included such categories as best kiss and best fight. The show, hosted by Mike Myers at the Barker Hangar in the Los Angeles suburb of Santa Monica, will air in the United States on June 12 on the music cable network. MTV's various international channels will screen it in the next few weeks.

Carrey's awards were for best villain and best comedic performance. When his name was announced for the villain award, he jumped from his seat and ran away from the stage, high-fiving audience members along the way.

When he finally reached the podium, he thanked the executives at Sony Pictures who greenlighted the picture and were subsequently fired in a studio restructuring. He concluded with: "I'll remember this not as an award, but as undeniable proof that I am a badass mother------"
Before exiting the stage to rousing applause, he made a lewd gesture by jerking his hand in front of his crotch.
Later in the evening, when he accepted the comedic performance trophy, he began a rambling speech by singing the chorus to George Thorogood's "Bad To the Bone," and then belching.
"When 'The Cable Guy' came out," he said, "I got a lot of criticism about it being 'too dark. Oh, it's not regular Jim Carrey fare.' But I'm not bitter!"

Carrey missed out on a third trip to the stage when he lost in the best fight category (in which he was nominated with "The Cable Guy" co-star Matthew Broderick) to Fairuza Balk and Robin Tunney of the witchcraft horror movie, "The Craft".

The two-hour ceremony had several x-rated elements, which are likely to be excised when the show is televised. At the outset Myers dropped his trousers during a routine and simulated sex with a dancer.
Later, presenter Samuel L. Jackson referred to Carrey's first speech by saying, "Jim, funny mother------; Sam, bad mother------."
Backstage Myers told reporters he thought the show was still a bit too safe. "I don't think it was sexually explicit enough. I like my comedy porno."

In the other categories: the teen slasher flick "Scream" won for best movie; Tom Cruise won best male performance for "Jerry Maguire" and the female award went to Claire Danes of "William Shakespeare's Romeo & Juliet".
Matthew McConaughey won the breakthrough performance trophy for his role as a Mississippi attorney in the courtroom drama, "A Time To Kill".

Best kiss went to Will Smith and Vivica A. Fox for "Independence Day," despite strong competition from Gina Gershon and Jennifer Tilly in the lesbian gangster movie, "Bound." Backstage Smith doubted his girlfriend, Jada Pinkett, would be concerned by his honour.
"Jada knows that I deserve awards for my kissing anyway. I think she'll just be happy that the rest of the world finally knows."

MTV's own Beavis and Butt-head, the animated stars of "Beavis and Butt-head Do America", lost in the best on-screen duo category to Nicolas Cage and Sean Connery for the tense action drama, "The Rock".
Best action sequence went to a scene from "Twister." British rockers Bush, who performed at the ceremony, won best song for "Machinehead" from the movie, "Fear."
Winners of the awards were determined by a national poll of MTV viewers, who were able to cast their votes through a special phone line and through MTV Online.

In special categories, "Swingers" director Doug Liman won the best new filmmaker award. He was chosen by students from several film schools around the United States. The show organisers honoured Chewbacca, the hirsute fighter pilot from the "Star Wars" trilogy, with a lifetime achievement award presented by co-star Carrie Fisher, who play Princess Leia.
